factors.name: Starlink growth
factors.line: 13.6M consumer subs, +89% y/y; the profit engine
why: Subscribers nearly doubled in a year and Connectivity is the most profitable segment.
Direct-to-cell (22M monthly users) and a 2027 terrestrial 5G network widen the market.
Drag: consumer ARPU fell from $83 to $69 a month year on year, and users report price hikes.

news.title: Barclays: T-Mobile is the 'cleanest' carrier if SpaceX buys one
Qualcomm Dragonwing picked for Starlink Mobile 5G, rollout from 2027
Users report capacity-based price hikes, some plans $156/month

factors.name: Starship and launch-cost lead
factors.line: 90% of global mass to orbit; full reuse attempt Nov 13
why: No one else lands and reuses orbital boosters at this cadence; Blue Origin is grounded until Jan 2027.
Starship V3 reached orbit on Flight 14 and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (26 Tbps).
Flight 15 tries the first-ever catch of both stages. Success is the real cost unlock; failure delays it.

factors.name: AI space data centers
factors.line: The 10X+ unlock, but physics and cost are unproven
why: This is the one driver big enough to justify 10X and above, so its weight grows with the horizon.
Plans are real (FCC filing for up to 1M satellites; prospectus goal 100 GW/year), but nothing is approved or flying at scale.
Independent analyses say orbit costs at least 10x more per GPU-year today; Google sees parity only in the mid-2030s.

factors.name: SpaceXAI: xAI, Grok, Cursor
factors.line: Now over half of revenue; growth bought with huge capex
why: xAI is fully part of SpaceX since Feb 2026; Cursor added in Aug. AI revenue went from $0.8B to $7.6B a quarter.
A $63B backlog and Q1 2027 guidance of $33–37B show real contracted demand.
Against: Q4 capex of $35–40B, related-party GPU leases, and a crowded AI race.

metrics.value: 1.7 GW now; 2.5–3 GW targeted by end of Q4

Musk: over $100B annualized revenue by Dec 2026, $500B ARR by end-2027 as best guess

factors.name: Own chips: Terafab
factors.line: SpaceX–Tesla joint fab; test chip mid-2027, volume 2028 at best
why: Own chip supply would cut dependence on Nvidia for both ground and orbital compute.
It is a joint venture with Tesla, not SpaceX-only, and Musk himself puts 'big error bars' on the dates.
No confirmed EUV tool orders; cutting-edge US fabs usually take three years or more.

news.title: Musk: ASML and others expediting chipmaking gear for Terafab

factors.name: Financials and profitability
factors.line: First profit in Q3; revenue tripled Q1 to Q3
why: Q3 brought a $4.4B net profit and $8.8B adjusted EBITDA; next-quarter guidance more than doubles revenue again.
Consensus 2027 EPS jumped to $4.10, which puts the stock at about 35x 2027 earnings (own arithmetic).
Against: trailing 12-month net income is still negative, and capex is rising faster than revenue.

news.title: Q3 results: revenue +161%, first quarterly profit

factors.name: Vertical integration
factors.line: Launch, satellites, network and AI under one roof
why: SpaceX builds its own rockets, satellites, laser mesh, ground compute and AI models, and launches 23 of its own missions a quarter.
That stack is what makes orbital compute even thinkable; no rival has all the pieces.
Risk: everything depends on Starship; a delay there ripples through Starlink V3 and orbital compute.

metrics.label: Starlink V3 per Starship
metrics.value: 26 satellites, equal to about 10 Falcon 9 launches

factors.name: Macro and interest rates
factors.line: Fed hiked in Sep; markets price about 80% odds of a Dec hike
why: Long-duration growth stocks suffer most when rates rise; SPCX is priced on profits years away.
The Fed is at 3.75–4.00% after a September hike, with two dissents for another hike in October.
Mostly a 1-year factor; over 10 years the business matters more than the rate cycle.

news.title: Fed holds; Cook and Hammack dissent in favor of a hike

factors.name: Nasdaq and AI-sector sentiment
factors.line: Post-midterm AI selloff, then a sharp two-day rebound
why: SPCX trades as an AI-infrastructure stock now; it fell to $123.62 on Nov 5 on fears that the midterm result slows data center buildout.
It bounced 15% in two sessions as tech recovered, with the Nasdaq up 2.3% on Nov 9.
Daily swings of 5–15% are common; a low float and unlocks amplify sector moves.

news.title: ARK bought $96M of SPCX; Stifel Buy, $190 target
SpaceX added over $100B of value in one day

factors.name: Valuation vs peers
factors.line: About 60x trailing sales; much is already priced in
why: At $1.93T SpaceX is valued above Meta and Tesla on a fraction of their revenue.
The analyst average target is $255, but the stock already hit $225 in June and fell back.
Rapid earnings growth could compress the multiple without the price falling, which is the bull path.

factors.name: Share unlocks and insider selling
factors.line: About 17% more shares unlock on Dec 8–9; Musk in June 2027
why: The float was about 5% at the IPO; staged unlocks have released supply in waves.
The Oct 22 unlock of 1.3B shares coincided with a 9% one-day drop; the August one was followed by a rally.
A pure timing factor: little effect beyond 2027.

news.title: December unlock nearly the biggest in IPO history

factors.name: Index inclusion
factors.line: In the Nasdaq-100; S&P 500 possible from June 2027
why: Nasdaq-100 funds had to buy in July; its weight is 2.82% after the September rebalance.
S&P 500 needs 12 months of trading and positive GAAP profit over four quarters; Q3's profit makes a mid-2027 entry plausible.
S&P inclusion would force large passive buying, a 2027 catalyst.

metrics.label: Four-quarter GAAP test
metrics.value: Not yet met; passes if Q4 2026 net income tops about $0.41B (tape.panke.app)

factors.name: Regulation: FCC, FAA, spectrum, permits
factors.line: Million-satellite filing pending; Memphis turbines under legal fire
why: Orbital compute needs approvals that the prospectus itself says may never come.
Each Starship flight needs FAA sign-off; Flight 15 is 'pending regulatory approval'.
Data center power is contested: the NAACP sued over gas turbines in Memphis; Starbase tax deals face review Dec 9.

factors.name: Geopolitics and defense contracts
factors.line: Golden Dome backbone and tracking satellites; NASA moon base
why: SpaceX holds the Space Data Network Backbone ($2.29B) and a $4.16B tracking-satellite award tied to Golden Dome.
NASA's $10B+ moon base awards include SpaceX.
Against: dependence on US politics, and friction with Europe that favors 'sovereign' rivals.

factors.name: Competition: Amazon Leo, China, Blue Origin
factors.line: Rivals are years behind today, but well funded
why: Amazon Leo has 396 satellites and no public service; China's two constellations total 514; Starlink has over 11,000.
Blue Origin reused a booster in April but has been grounded since a May pad explosion.
Long-term threat: price competition for Starlink and state-backed rivals in markets closed to SpaceX.

metrics.label: Amazon Leo
metrics.value: 396 satellites; service planned late 2026; first Vulcan launch Nov 13

metrics.label: Orbital compute rivals
metrics.value: Google Suncatcher demo early 2027; Starcloud 88,000-satellite filing

factors.name: Musk: key-man, attention, politics
factors.line: Delivers the hard things, usually years late; controls the votes
why: Musk is CEO, Chief Engineer and Chairman, also runs Tesla, and holds about 82% of SpaceX votes.
Track record: reusable rockets and Starlink delivered; FSD, robotaxi and Mars dates missed by years.
Political exposure cuts both ways: defense contracts on one side, EU friction and boycotts on the other.

factors.name: Tesla linkage and merger talk
factors.line: Special committees exploring a deal; no terms
why: A combination would create a company of about $3.4T, close to the #1 spot, but by combining rather than growing.
Tesla supplies Megapacks and solar to SpaceX data centers and co-owns Terafab.
Analysts at William Blair see the merger as mostly about Musk's control; it needs 50% of all Tesla shares.

pillars.name: Cheapest launch system
for: 90% of global mass to orbit in Q3 2026.
Falcon booster reuse is routine; Starship V3 reached orbit with 26 Starlink V3 satellites.
Nearest rival Blue Origin is grounded until January 2027.
against: Starship is not yet fully reusable; the first ship catch is Nov 13.
No official cost per kg; Flight 14 had engine-loss issues.

pillars.name: Starlink as the cash engine
for: $2.37B operating income in Q3; 22M direct-to-cell users.
Defense awards of $2.29B and $4.16B on Starshield.
against: Consumer ARPU fell from $83 to $69 a month.
Amazon Leo and two Chinese constellations are coming; T-Mobile refuses a SpaceX MVNO.

pillars.name: Own chip supply
for: Terafab broke ground in Aug 2026; $16.8B first phase; Intel on board; ASML expediting tools.
against: Shared with Tesla, not SpaceX alone.
Test chip mid-2027, volume Q3–Q4 2028 at best; Musk: 'big error bars'.
Today's compute runs on Nvidia GB300s.

pillars.name: AI space data centers
for: FCC filing accepted; prospectus calls 10 GW/year commercially attractive.
Only SpaceX has heavy reusable launch, a satellite factory and a laser mesh together.
against: Not approved; first shells 'by the end of the decade'.
ABI: at least 10x the cost of a ground GPU today; radiators and radiation are hard limits.
Google's own paper: parity only in the mid-2030s.

pillars.name: AI business on the ground (xAI, Grok, Cursor)
for: AI revenue $7.6B in Q3, from $0.8B a year earlier; $63B backlog.
against: Q4 capex of $35–40B; over $20B of related-party GPU leases.
Competes with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; NAACP lawsuit over Memphis turbines.

pillars.name: Result: most valuable company ever
for: Already #6–7 in the world at $1.93T; needs about 2.6x to pass Apple's $5.10T.
Revenue tripled from Q1 to Q3 2026.
against: The leaders keep growing too; 'ever' means holding the spot, not touching it.
Two of the four pillars are still plans; Musk's dates usually slip by years.
